html:
The Northern Yuki were the inland Yuki of the Eel River country in Mendocino County, northern California, centred on Round Valley; the Coast Yuki lived to their west. Their Yukian language is unrelated to the languages of their neighbours.

They lived in small villages, gathering acorns and catching salmon. In 1856 the United States set up a reservation in Round Valley, and between 1856 and 1864 settlers and state-backed militias carried out mass killings of the Yuki, part of the violence after the Gold Rush that many historians call the California genocide. The Yuki fell from thousands to a few hundred. Their descendants are part of the Round Valley Indian Tribes, along with Wailaki, Pomo and others moved there.
